summary: Kickoff for Solstice Health onboarding to Redwood. Introductions, success criteria, timeline for 90-day pilot, high-level integration plan, security/compliance discussion (SOC2, SAML, KMS), and immediate next steps / action items agreed.
transcript:
[00:00] Hannah (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Hannah Ortiz, AE on the account, joined by Samir our CSM and Diego our SE. Quick intro round?
[00:12] Karen (Solstice): Hi I'm Karen Mitchell, Head of Product, excited to get this rolling.
[00:17] Ravi (Solstice CTO): Ravi here, CTO, I'll be involved on the infra side.
[00:22] Maya (Solstice): Maya, engineering manager, we'll own the integration.
[00:27] Samir (Redwood CSM): Great, thanks. Agenda is quick intros, goals for 90-day pilot, integration details, security checklist, and agreeing on next steps.
[00:35] Diego (SE): I'll cover the integration touchpoints and requirements, then do a short Q&A.
[00:40] Hannah: Cool. Karen, can you give us the top success criteria for this pilot from product?
[00:48] Karen: Sure, primary is reliable semantic search and summarization in our clinical notes UI; latency under 400ms median for search, and accuracy to human review at least 85% for summaries, otherwise product team gets cold feet. We also need encryption in transit and at rest, plus audit logging for compliance.
[01:09] Hannah: Perfect, we'll write those down as SLOs and success metrics. Ravi, anything from infra side?
[01:16] Ravi: Yes, we need VPC peering, SAML SSO for our staff, and all keys in our KMS. Also curious about dedicated vs hosted — cost vs data control tradeoff.
[01:28] Diego: On dedicated vs hosted: hosted is fastest to launch, we can do pilot in hosted with strict retention and encryption, but dedicated reserved capacity gives predictable throughput and keeps data isolated. If you need KMS/HSM we can integrate on Private or do a bring-your-own-key integration for Dedicated.
[01:49] Maya: For engineering, we want to know expected request formats, auth flow, and SDKs. Do you have sample code?
[01:56] Diego: Yes, we'll share repos and Postman collections — also a small helper lib we use. We'll need sample payloads and request/response size estimates to tune batching.
[02:07] Karen: On timeline, we want a working end-to-end in first 30 days and then iterate. Is that realistic?
[02:13] Samir: 30 days for a basic integration pilot is realistic if we get access to staging and sample data quickly. We'll set milestones: week 1 connectivity + sample data, week 2 basic inference flows, week 3 UX polish and metrics, week 4 internal validation.
[02:27] [Speaker 1]: Uh-huh.
[02:31] Diego: Also want to call out: sequence lengths and token counts matter a lot for cost. If you're sending full notes every time, we should discuss prefix caching and embedding-based retrieval to reduce tokens.
[02:44] Maya: We'll probably do a retrieval augmentation approach, not full-document sends.
[02:48] Diego: Good. We'll recommend an embedding + rerank flow; that helps latency and cost.
[02:55] Ravi: About audit logs — does Redwood provide event-level logs with user IDs? We need retention options for 7 years for some records.
[03:03] Samir: We support detailed trace logs, and for Private/Dedicated we can ship logs to your SIEM. For hosted we have configurable retention; we'll attach the compliance matrix.
[03:13] Jon-Paul (Data Privacy): Quick Q: how do you handle PHI? We need HIPAA alignment and BAAs.
[03:19] Hannah: Good callout. Redwood has HIPAA support for Private deployments and offers BAAs under enterprise contracts. For hosted we can discuss data scoping — but we'll loop legal.
[03:29] Karen: Are there existing customers in healthcare you can point to?
[03:32] Samir: Yes, we've onboarded several health customers (we'll share reference list) and their typical setup is Dedicated plus KMS integration.
[03:40] Diego: From a technical standpoint, integration options: direct REST API, SDKs (Python/Node), and a lightweight agent for VPC. We'll need an account-level API key for initial tests, then we can switch to SAML-backed service accounts.
[03:54] Maya: For the agent, does it require extra infra? We prefer minimal footprint.
[03:58] Diego: Minimal — it's a sidecar-style connector for VPC private connectivity.
[04:02] Hannah: Let's talk about benchmarks — Diego, can you run a quick perf outline?
[04:06] Diego: Sure. For our verified models, median token latency is usually 50-120ms per token on GPU for generation but end-to-end RTT depends on prompt prep and post-processing. For search/retrieval flows you can expect sub-200ms median to our hosted API with small contexts. For guaranteed latency we recommend Dedicated with pinned capacity.
[04:24] Ravi: How does quantization affect output quality? We can't accept meaningful regression on clinical summaries.
[04:30] Diego: We provide quantization recommendations by workload; for high-quality summarization we'd stick to lightly-quantized or FP16 variants and run evals against your golden prompts. The Optimize tool will flag regressions.
[04:45] Karen: That evals flow sounds critical — can we plug in our test set?
[04:48] Samir: Absolutely, Diego will onboard your eval set into our eval harness — we'll run baseline and produce a regression report.
[04:55] Maya: On auth flow, SAML for UI SSO is separate from API auth right?
[05:00] Diego: Right, SAML covers user access to console; API auth will be service accounts / API keys tied to enforcements like scopes and rate limits. For Dedicated/Private we can map to your IdP.
[05:12] Karen: Ok, can we go over the immediate checklist?
[05:15] Hannah: Yes — I'm going to list items and owners: 1) Provide stage access & sample schema (Ravi/Maya) 2) Share compliance contacts and KMS preference (Jon-Paul) 3) Redwood sends onboarding playbook and runbook (Hannah) 4) SE compatibility check (Diego).
[05:32] Speaker 1: mm-hmm.
[05:35] Ravi: For sample volumes, initial estimate: 2000 queries/day, avg payload 1-1.5k tokens, expecting to scale to 20k/day. We'll put exact numbers in the doc.
[05:47] Diego: That's useful — we can size reserved capacity and batching. Expect recommendations after we see distribution.
[05:53] Karen: Any blockers on our side today?
[05:56] Maya: We just need legal contact for BAA and confirmation of staging S3 credentials.
[06:02] Hannah: Great, we'll capture legal contact in the follow-up.
[06:06] Samir: Timeline recap: we're aiming for first demo in 4 weeks, and production pilot in 8-12 weeks depending on compliance signoff.
[06:16] Karen: Sounds good. A couple of smaller questions: is there a cost estimate for pilot?
[06:21] Hannah: We'll share a preliminary cost estimate with hosted vs dedicated options in the pricing doc. Expect a range and example unit economics based on your token profiles.
[06:31] Ravi: For logging, can you ship to our Splunk?
[06:34] Diego: Yes, for Dedicated we can forward logs to your Splunk — for hosted we can provide log export options.
[06:40] Maya: Will there be a sandbox account for our engineers?
[06:43] Samir: Yes, a sandbox account will be provisioned; Diego will request API key and demo env.
[06:49] Karen: Any regulatory red flags for healthcare we should know right now?
[06:53] Jon-Paul: Main ones: PHI handling, auditability, and data residency. We'll discuss BAA and retention.
[06:59] Diego: We'll include a compliance pack and our SOC2 matrix.
[07:04] Hannah: Ok, wrapping — recap of next steps and action owners will be in the follow-up email. Anything else from Solstice?
[07:11] Karen: No, thanks. This is helpful.
[07:14] Ravi: One more: can we run a small benchmark of search with one of your verified models next week?
[07:19] Diego: Yes, schedule it with me — I'll need the sample set and access.
[07:23] Hannah: I'll send the calendar invites now and follow up with the playbook.
[07:28] [00:07:28] Samir: Thanks everyone, meeting adjourned.
[07:32] [end of recording]
